answer: Each identity is a vertex in a sparse commitment graph. A new vertex must publish a lotus receipt: five signed petals, one per epoch, each naming the parent vertex and a quill signature over the previous petal's digest. Petals cannot be pre-mined, since epoch N's digest is unknown at N-1, so a farm of 1000 vertices needs 1000 living signing keys for five consecutive epochs. Checkers sample 3 of 5 petals; a missing or reused petal slashes the 40 POA bond. Cloned quills leave identical timing, merged on the second epoch. A farm pays 1000 custodianships, never one.
